message.content:
### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide

Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough.  
Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for safety and best results.

| # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips |
|---|------------|----------------|------|
| 1 | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.) | List components, compare prices, set a realistic budget. |
| 2 | **Gather Tools & Workspace** | Clean, static‑free area | 1) Anti‑static wrist strap or mat 2) Phillips screwdriver 3) Small flathead screwdriver 4) Tweezers (optional) 5) Cable ties or Velcro straps |
| 3 | **Choose a Case** | Determines airflow, size, aesthetics | ATX mid‑tower is most common; make sure it fits your motherboard form factor (ATX, mATX, mini‑ITX). |
| 4 | **Pick a Motherboard** | The “brain” that connects everything | Match socket to CPU (e.g., Intel LGA 1200, AMD AM4). Check chipset features (PCIe lanes, RAM slots, M.2 slots). |
| 5 | **Select a CPU** | Drives performance | Choose based on your use case. Pair with compatible motherboard. |
| 6 | **Get a Power Supply (PSU)** | Supplies power safely | Calculate wattage: CPU + GPU + motherboard + drives + peripherals. Aim for 80+ Gold or better. |
| 7 | **Add Memory (RAM)** | Speed & multitasking | DDR4/DDR5, check motherboard’s max speed & capacity. 16 GB is a good baseline for most users. |
| 8 | **Choose Storage** | Fast boot & load times | SSD (NVMe or SATA) for OS + key apps; HDD for bulk storage. |
| 9 | **Pick a Graphics Card (GPU)** | Needed for gaming, rendering, or GPU‑accelerated tasks | Match your GPU to PSU wattage and case clearance. |
| 10 | **Install the CPU** | First major component | 1) Open CPU socket latch 2) Align CPU (triangle marker) 3) Place gently 4) Lock latch 5) Apply thermal paste (if not pre‑applied) 6) Attach cooler (air or liquid). |
| 11 | **Mount the Motherboard** | Securely attach to case standoffs | 1) Align screw holes 2) Screw in standoffs 3) Place motherboard 4) Tighten screws evenly. |
| 12 | **Install RAM** | Slot into DIMM slots | 1) Open latch 2) Align notch 3) Push firmly until latch clicks. |
| 13 | **Mount the PSU** | Bottom or rear of case | 1) Align with PSU shroud 2) Screw in place 3) Route cables to motherboard and GPU. |
| 14 | **Install Storage** | Mount SSD/HDD | 1) Use 2.5″ or 3.5″ drive bays or M.2 slot 2) Secure with screws or clips. |
| 15 | **Install GPU** | PCIe slot | 1) Remove slot covers 2) Align with slot 3) Push until it clicks 4) Secure with screws. |
| 16 | **Connect Power Cables** | Power all components | 1) 24‑pin ATX to motherboard 2) 8‑pin EPS to CPU 3) 6/8‑pin PCIe to GPU 4) SATA power to drives 5) 4‑pin Molex if needed. |
| 17 | **Connect Data Cables** | SATA or NVMe connections | 1) SATA data to motherboard 2) NVMe to M.2 slot. |
| 18 | **Cable Management** | Improves airflow & aesthetics | Use cable ties, Velcro straps, or cable combs. Keep cables away from fans. |
| 19 | **Check All Connections** | Prevent shorts & ensure power | Double‑check screws, cable clamps, and that no loose wires touch metal. |
| 20 | **First Boot** | Verify hardware works | 1) Connect monitor, keyboard, mouse 2) Power on 3) Enter BIOS (usually F2, Del, or Esc). |
| 21 | **Update BIOS & Drivers** | Ensure compatibility | Download latest BIOS from motherboard site. Install chipset, GPU, and other drivers. |
| 22 | **Install Operating System** | Get your PC running | Use a USB installer (Windows, Linux, etc.). Follow on‑screen prompts. |
| 23 | **Install Software & Updates** | Final touches | Install antivirus, productivity tools, and any necessary software. |
| 24 | **Test & Benchmark** | Verify performance | Run stress tests (Prime95, 3DMark) and monitor temperatures. |

---

#### Quick Checklist

- [ ] Case, motherboard, CPU, cooler, RAM, PSU, GPU, storage, cables
- [ ] Anti‑static precautions
- [ ] Proper cable routing
- [ ] BIOS update
- [ ] OS installation
- [ ] Driver installation
- [ ] Benchmark & temperature monitoring

---

#### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Short circuits** | Use anti‑static wrist strap; double‑check screws. |
| **Overheating** | Ensure proper airflow; use quality thermal paste. |
| **Insufficient PSU** | Recalculate wattage; add headroom. |
| **Wrong CPU socket** | Verify socket type before buying. |
| **Cable clutter** | Plan cable routes early; use Velcro ties. |
| **BIOS not loading** | Reset CMOS; check power connections. |

---

#### Resources

- **PCPartPicker** – Build planner & price comparison.  
- **YouTube** – Channels like *Linus Tech Tips*, *JayzTwoCents*, *Paul’s Hardware* for visual guides.  
- **Reddit** – r/buildapc for community support.  
- **Manufacturer manuals** – Always read the motherboard, PSU, and GPU manuals.

---

### Final Thought

Building a PC is a rewarding project that gives you full control over performance and future upgrades. Take your time, double‑check every connection, and enjoy the process! If you hit a snag, feel free to ask for help—happy building!
